proposals.title: Account-scope local state
proposals.currentState: One global localStorage key `vizion.ui.v1` persists `editorDraft` (raw prompt text), theme, mode, target, thinkingLevels. IndexedDB `vizion-outbox` items carry no userId. Cache Storage `vizion-shell` is global. Sign-out clears cookies only.

src/stores/ui.ts:152-158 — partialize persists editorDraft
src/app/auth/sign-out/route.ts:5-11 — signOut() + redirect; no local purge

src/components/pwa/OutboxFlusher.tsx:39-44 — flushes on mount/online/visibilitychange
src/components/ProfileHydrator.tsx:22-26 — resets only theme + targetModel on sign-in
proposals.argumentFor: Cross-account data leak and cross-account WRITE on any shared device. User A queues a save offline and signs out; User B signs in; OutboxFlusher replays A's payload and savePromptAction writes it into B's library. B also inherits A's draft prompt text in the composer.
proposals.argumentAgainst: Requires a shared device; single-user installs are unaffected. Partitioning keys is a migration that can strand existing drafts.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Ship the purge first (clear store + outbox + caches on sign-out) — that alone closes the write path — then add userId scoping and owner-checked replay.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A test signing in as two users and asserting zero carry-over of draft, outbox, and cache. If replay were already owner-checked this would drop to P1.

proposals.title: Atomic spend enforcement
proposals.currentState: Cap is a read-then-act: `usage_window` RPC reads settled today_cost, compares to COST_CAP_USD_PER_DAY, then the provider runs ~30 lines later. Ledger insert happens in `finally` AFTER the run. No reservation, no lock, no per-request maximum, no idempotency key.
evidence: src/app/api/enhance/route.ts:111-126 — the read-then-act check, quoted in the report
src/app/api/enhance/route.ts:156 — provider first touched here
src/app/api/enhance/route.ts:236-244 — ledger INSERT inside finally
src/app/api/media/route.ts:90-101 — identical shape
src/lib/security/rate-limit.ts:7-8 — in-memory limiter self-documented as not authoritative across instances
tasks/lessons.md — a prior 22P02 incident already made ledger writes fail silently, disabling the cap for 4 models
proposals.argumentFor: Billing exposure. With the $2 default cap at $1.99 spent, N concurrent requests all read $1.99 and all proceed; a fable_5 run at $50/1M out against a 64k ceiling is ~$3.20, so a 20-request burst can settle ~$64 against a $2 cap (~32x). A single request is never bounded against remaining headroom either.
proposals.argumentAgainst: Real-world concurrency for one user is low, and Vercel's per-instance limiter incidentally dampens it. Atomic reservation adds a write to the hot path and needs refund logic.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Add a per-request projected-cost ceiling and reject when today_cost + maxProjected > cap. That bounds worst case without a full reservation ledger; two-phase reservation is the complete fix.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A concurrency test firing N simultaneous requests near the cap and asserting total settled spend stays within cap + one max-request.

proposals.argumentFor: Prices set the cost cap. A silently stale price or a floating alias that moves under a pinned price makes the cap wrong in a direction nobody notices until the invoice.

proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: Confirmation that deployed PRICE_* env overrides match the registry defaults would narrow this to the alias-pinning half.

proposals.title: Bound quadratic diffing
proposals.currentState: diffWords is a full dynamic-programming LCS materializing an (n+1)x(m+1) number table. No token cap, no fallback, no worker. Runs synchronously on the server event loop and unmemoized in a client render body.
evidence: src/lib/enhance/diff.ts:35-37 — Array.from({length:n+1}) of Array(m+1), full table
src/lib/enhance/diff.ts:23-27 — self-described 'O(n·m) which is fine for prompt-sized inputs'
src/lib/enhance/diff.ts:19-21 — tokenizer keeps whitespace as tokens, ~2x n and m
src/app/api/enhance/route.ts:190-199 — called synchronously inside the SSE start callback
src/components/library/PromptDetail.tsx:86 — called in render body, NOT memoized
src/app/api/enhance/route.ts:30 — MAX_INPUT_CHARS=20_000 bounds input only; output is unbounded
tests/unit/diff.test.ts — correctness only, no size or timing test
proposals.argumentFor: A legal 20k-char input against a 16k-token output builds a table on the order of 10^8 cells across thousands of Array objects — hundreds of MB and many seconds — while blocking the serverless event loop. In the library, diffWords runs on EVERY keystroke in the revise textarea.
proposals.argumentAgainst: Typical prompts are small, so the ceiling is rarely reached in practice; the useMemo half is a one-line fix that removes most real-world pain.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Wrap the client call in useMemo (one line, immediate) and add an n*m ceiling that falls back to line-level diff above the bound. Worker execution only if profiling still shows a problem.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A benchmark at 20k x 16k showing acceptable time and memory would downgrade this; measured multi-second blocking confirms it.

proposals.title: No private authenticated HTML in caches
proposals.currentState: The service worker's single runtime route matches same-origin navigations under StaleWhileRevalidate, so authenticated HTML for /enhance, /library, /library/[id], /profile is written to the `vizion-shell` cache and served stale-first on later navigations. Purge fires only when /sign-in loads as a fresh navigation.
evidence: src/lib/pwa/sw-src.js:72-76 — isShellAsset returns true for request.mode === 'navigate'
src/lib/pwa/sw-src.js:78-87 — StaleWhileRevalidate into SHELL_CACHE
src/lib/pwa/register-sw.ts:43-51 — purge only when location.pathname === '/sign-in'
src/middleware.ts — every app route is auth-gated, so all cached navigations are private
RSC (?_rsc=) requests fall through to network — destination '' and mode !== navigate
proposals.argumentFor: Another user of the same device can be served the previous user's rendered Library and Profile HTML from Cache Storage before any revalidation completes. The purge depends on a full-page load of /sign-in and does not fire on a client-side route change or a silently expired session.
proposals.argumentAgainst: The stale window is short and revalidation corrects it; removing navigation caching costs the offline-reopen behavior for authenticated pages.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Network-first (or no-store) for navigations, keeping SWR for script/style/font/image only; purge the shell cache from the sign-out path directly rather than inferring it from a pathname.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: Evidence that navigations are already excluded, or that the purge fires reliably on every sign-out path including expiry.

proposals.title: Reproducible database baseline
proposals.currentState: All 7 migrations are single-statement ALTER TYPE. The repository contains zero CREATE TABLE, zero CREATE POLICY, zero ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, zero storage policy, and zero CREATE FUNCTION — including `usage_window`, which is the only durable spend and rate guardrail. A fresh rebuild fails on migration 1 because the enum it alters was never created.
evidence: supabase/migrations/ — 7 files, every one a single ALTER TYPE
grep across supabase/ for CREATE TABLE|CREATE POLICY|ROW LEVEL SECURITY|CREATE FUNCTION returns nothing
docs/runbooks/migrations.md:23-30 — states the P2-P5 base schema 'exists only in its migration ledger' on the hosted project
src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts:264-269 — usage_window declared in types, body nowhere in repo
docs/runbooks/hardening.md:6-8 — RLS asserted in prose only
docs/architecture.md:95 — claims policy shape auth.uid() = user_id, but prompt_versions has no user_id column
proposals.argumentFor: There is no disaster-recovery path from source control and no way to stand up a test environment. RLS — the entire authorization model — is unreviewable, untestable, and unversioned. The documented policy shape cannot even express ownership for prompt_versions or media_assets.
proposals.argumentAgainst: The hosted project works today and Supabase PITR exists, so this is latent rather than actively breaking.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Dump the hosted schema (pg_dump --schema-only including policies and functions) into a baseline migration, then add an ephemeral rebuild + RLS assertion job to CI.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A successful fresh-project rebuild from supabase/migrations alone would overturn this outright.

proposals.title: Transactional Library mutations
proposals.currentState: All six library server actions are sequences of independent statements with no transaction. savePromptAction discards the return of the current_ver UPDATE and the activity inserts. addVersionAction reads current_ver then writes it as parent_ver in a separate round trip. restoreVersionAction never validates that versionId belongs to promptId.
evidence: src/lib/library/actions.ts:53-91 — savePromptAction, 4 unguarded statements
src/lib/library/actions.ts:82 — UPDATE current_ver, return value discarded
src/lib/library/actions.ts:111-131 — read-then-write race on parent_ver
src/lib/library/actions.ts:160-165 — restore updates current_ver with an unvalidated versionId
src/lib/library/actions.ts:181-191, 210-216 — updateTags/delete never call auth.getUser()
src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts — Relationships: [] on all seven tables (no declared FKs)
proposals.argumentFor: Partial failure leaves orphan prompts with current_ver NULL that the user retries into duplicates; concurrent revisions fork the version DAG silently; restore can point prompt A at a version of prompt B unless an FK that the generated types say does not exist actually does.
proposals.argumentAgainst: RLS still scopes every row to the owner, so this is integrity damage rather than a cross-account breach.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Move each mutation into a single Postgres function with ownership checks and stable result codes — which requires DB-01's baseline to exist first.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: Confirmation that FK constraints exist in the hosted DB would defuse the restore path; the orphan and race paths stand regardless.

proposals.title: Revision/run integrity
proposals.currentState: Save correctly uses a submitted snapshot, not the live draft — EnhanceComposer captures {input, mode, target} at request time. But Revise seeds its textarea from current.input_text (the ORIGINAL prompt), not the improved output, and useState never re-seeds after a save or restore. There are no immutable run IDs.
evidence: src/components/editor/EnhanceComposer.tsx:56-64 — submitted snapshot captured at request time (this half is correct)
src/components/library/PromptDetail.tsx:91 — useState(current?.input_text) seeds Revise from the original
src/components/library/PromptDetail.tsx:97 — the sibling copy action uses output_text, so the distinction is deliberate
src/components/library/PromptDetail.tsx:76-82 — re-seed effect updates only aId/bId, never draft/mode
No run_id column exists on prompt_versions
proposals.argumentFor: The prompt's stated north star is 'revise' the improvement. Today Revise re-runs the original with different settings, and after saving a revision the textarea still holds the previous version's input — a stale-state bug independent of the semantic question.
proposals.argumentAgainst: Re-running the original is a defensible product choice (it produces siblings, not a degrading chain); changing it silently would alter existing user expectations.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Fix the non-controversial half first: re-seed draft/mode when current changes. Then offer an explicit 'start from improved output' toggle rather than switching the default.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A product decision that sibling-branching is intended would reduce this to the re-seed bug alone.

proposals.title: Trustworthy media retention/quota
proposals.currentState: The 50 MB quota is enforced only in client-side JS; there is no server upload route — the browser writes straight to Supabase Storage. No retention, TTL, or cleanup of any kind. Delete removes the storage object first, then the row; a row-delete failure leaves an orphan row whose bytes count against quota forever. File extension is taken unsanitised from user input. The avatars bucket is public.
evidence: src/lib/media/formatters.ts:103 — MEDIA_QUOTA_BYTES = 50MB
src/lib/media/queue.ts:59-83 — admitFiles, a pure client-side function
src/components/media/MediaStudio.tsx:207-241 — direct client upload; ext from file.name.split('.').pop() unsanitised
src/components/media/MediaStudio.tsx:107-126 — storage delete then row delete, early return on row failure
src/components/profile/ProfilePanel.tsx:83-88 — avatars bucket written then read via getPublicUrl
No cron, scheduled function, or TTL anywhere in the repo
proposals.argumentFor: A client-only quota is not a quota — any direct storage call with the user's own session bypasses it, so storage cost is unbounded per user. Orphan rows permanently consume the user's visible quota with no repair path.
proposals.argumentAgainst: The media bucket is private and path-prefixed, so the exposure is cost and hygiene rather than confidentiality. Avatars being public is arguably intended.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Enforce the quota in a storage RLS policy or a signed-upload route; make delete idempotent and row-first so a failure cannot orphan.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: A storage policy that caps per-user bytes would resolve the quota half; documented intent would resolve the public-avatar question.

For polish/clarify the conventions are dropped entirely, so the target then affects only cost and routing.

proposals.argumentFor: Every downstream feature (Auto optimizer, destination variants, capability manifest, picker redesign) is blocked on separating these concepts. The conflation is already visible as an inconsistency: the same control means different things depending on mode.

proposals.title: Conditional clarification
proposals.currentState: No clarification step exists — every run goes straight to the provider. The eval confirms the model sometimes builds clarifying questions INTO the output prompt instead (the expand/short case produced 'ask me 7 questions'), which is a different thing.
evidence: src/app/api/enhance/route.ts — single-shot request, no interstitial
PROD-04 harness, expand/short case — the model embeds clarifying questions in the output rather than asking the user
proposals.argumentFor: For genuinely underspecified input ('fix this', 'make me a logo') the tool must either ask or state assumptions; today it silently invents a direction the user never sees.
proposals.argumentAgainst: An interstitial interrupts the one-action promise and risks becoming a form. Most inputs do not need it.
proposals.simplerAlternative: Ship the assumptions half only: have the model list the assumptions it made and render them above the result. No round trip, no interruption.
proposals.evidenceThatWouldChangeDecision: Eval evidence that assumption-listing alone resolves user confusion would make the question flow unnecessary.

proposals.title: Semantic quality evaluation gate
proposals.currentState: No eval set, rubric, or semantic gate exists in the repo or CI. The contract itself is defended by negative-substring unit tests only. This audit ran a 20-call harness against the real buildSystemPrompt output and the real production model: 0 envelope failures, 0 assertion failures.

Stage-1 harness, 2026-07-27, model gpt-5.6-sol, 20 calls, 9,002 in / 3,980 out tokens, $0.1047
Harness result: 0/20 envelope failures, 0 assertion failures across no-role-labels, shape-preservation, injection resistance, does-not-answer

proposals.argumentFor: The contract is good and currently holds — which is exactly what makes the absence of a regression net expensive. lessons.md records two production incidents (role framing, shape destruction) caused by contract edits; nothing today would catch a third.

newlyDiscovered.detail: ADR 0001 locks TanStack Query as the server-state layer, but there are zero useQuery calls in the codebase — the only usage is a single useMutation in use-enhance.ts. Data flows through RSC and server actions instead, so the configured staleTime, gcTime and networkMode are inert.
evidence: src/lib/query/provider.tsx:16-25
grep useQuery across src/ — zero hits
src/lib/enhance/use-enhance.ts:4,113 — the only useMutation
newlyDiscovered.fix: Either adopt it for client-side data or drop it and the provider, and update ADR 0001 to match reality.

newlyDiscovered.title: CSP retains script-src 'unsafe-inline' for the theme bootstrap
newlyDiscovered.detail: The pre-paint no-flash script in layout.tsx is inlined via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, which forces script-src 'unsafe-inline' in the CSP and materially weakens XSS defence app-wide. next.config.ts documents it as a known residual.
evidence: next.config.ts:11-13,15-30 — CSP and the documented residual
src/app/layout.tsx:39,50 — the inline bootstrap
Production response header confirms script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
newlyDiscovered.fix: Adopt a nonce for the bootstrap script, which Next supports via middleware, and drop 'unsafe-inline'.

newlyDiscovered.title: Streaming scanner can silently stop streaming on unusual provider whitespace
newlyDiscovered.detail: createEnvelopeScanner retains only field.length + 16 characters between chunks while seeking. A provider emitting "output" followed by a long whitespace run before the opening quote would slide past the retained window, so no deltas ever stream. Correctness is unaffected because parseEnhancePayload remains authoritative on the full text — the user would just see nothing until completion.
evidence: src/lib/providers/json-stream.ts:67
docs/decisions/0002-stream-inside-the-json-envelope.md:37-39 — the known degradation mode
newlyDiscovered.fix: Retain a slightly larger seek window or track the seek state across chunks rather than truncating.

newlyDiscovered.title: offline.html ignores the user's stored theme
newlyDiscovered.detail: The offline fallback page inlines its own tokens with a prefers-color-scheme override only. A user who explicitly chose light or dark against their OS preference sees the OS preference instead while offline.
evidence: public/offline.html:19-24
newlyDiscovered.fix: Read the same vizion.ui.v1 key the layout bootstrap reads, or accept the divergence deliberately.

newlyDiscovered.title: Unreferenced icon assets ship in public/icons
newlyDiscovered.detail: public/icons contains 19 PNGs; the manifest references 7. apple-touch-icon.png and the three favicons are unreferenced because Next serves src/app/icon.png, icon.svg and apple-icon.png via the metadata file convention instead.
evidence: public/icons/ — 19 files
public/manifest.webmanifest — 7 icon entries
Production HTML — icons resolve to /icon.png and /apple-icon.png
newlyDiscovered.fix: Remove the dead files or reference them; confirm against the generator so the next icon regeneration does not reintroduce them.
